name: assets_yes_resolves_applies
description: Opening question names the asset-transfer rule's evidence vocabulary ("assets"); an affirmative response-interjection satisfies the one Boolean slot and resolves the rule as applying.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for the assets
yes

name: assets_no_resolves_does_not_apply
description: Same opening question; a negative response-interjection resolves the rule as NOT applying.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for the assets
no

name: fair_market_value_yes_resolves_applies
description: A different content-word overlap ("fair market value", verbatim from the rule's own cited evidence text) opens the same rule.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for the fair market value
yes

name: spouse_no_resolves_does_not_apply
description: A third content-word overlap ("spouse") opens the same rule; resolves NOT applying.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for a spouse
no

name: subject_phrase_varies_predicate_still_routes
description: Varying the subject noun phrase ("the applicant" instead of "a widget") still reaches the predicate mechanism — the routing depends on the object's vocabulary overlap, not the subject.

turns.utterance: is the applicant eligible for the assets
yes

name: unrecognized_answer_reasks_then_resolves
description: An answer that is not a loaded response-interjection ("maybe") does not fabricate a parse — the session re-states the SAME pending question rather than guessing or dropping the frame. A later recognized answer resolves it normally.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for the assets
maybe
yes

name: unrelated_question_mid_frame_reasks_rather_than_switching_topic
description: While a rule is pending, an ordinary, well-formed but unrelated question ("what is a dog") is interpreted against the PENDING slot, not routed as a fresh question — it fails to parse as yes/no, so the session re-asks the same pending fact rather than silently abandoning the open frame.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for the assets
what is a dog
no

name: unrelated_eligibility_question_never_opens_a_frame
description: An "eligible for" question whose object shares no vocabulary with the registry rule's own cited evidence text must never open a rule frame — the topic-overlap gate (task #28), a single-turn control case restated in dialogue form.

turns.utterance: is a widget eligible for a benefit

name: real_corpus_shaped_eligibility_questions_never_misattribute
description: The shape of the real 4617-question corpus's actual "eligible for X" questions (named benefit programs, not asset transfers) — none may resolve to the asset-transfer rule, run here as three independent single-turn exchanges in one session to confirm no cross-turn state leaks between unrelated questions. `Abstained` is the correct, honest outcome: "eligible for" is recognized as a governance predicate (predicate_lexicon.rs), but no loaded rule covers Medicare/Medicaid/TennCare eligibility specifically, so the pipeline admits it doesn't have that rule rather than fabricating one. (Previously expected `Answered` — that captured the pre-fix pipeline's actual behavior, which was a WordNet-sense dump of "mother"/"eligible"/"medicare" via the same over-eager fallback the Track 2.3 fix corrected, not a genuine eligibility determination.)

turns.utterance: is my mother eligible for Medicare
is my mother eligible for Medicaid
is my mother eligible for TennCare

name: ordinary_questions_bracket_two_independent_resolved_frames
description: One session, in order: an ordinary define question, a rule opened and resolved Applies, an ordinary is-a question, then a SECOND independent rule opened and resolved DoesNotApply — proving a session behaves identically to a stateless call when no frame is pending (task #17's own doc claim) and that resolving one frame leaves the session ready for a wholly separate one.

turns.utterance: what is a dog
is a widget eligible for the assets
yes
is a dog an animal
is a widget eligible for a spouse
no
